messages:
Jamie: Heads-up — ran the 09:30 perf sweep and saw p99 spikes from the continuous batcher. Lots of short prompts getting mixed into the middle queue.

Rachel: Hmm, are you seeing mis-bucketing by prompt length or decode-rate grouping? :thinking:

Jamie: Decode-rate. Short prompts (~<80 tokens) that decode at ~35 tok/s were being grouped with med prompts. Token budget hit early and p99 jumped.

Mikhail: Can you paste a profiling sample and kernel selection trace for one of the slow batches?

Jamie: Pasting snippet from trace collector:
```
[2026-03-06T09:30:12Z] sample=42 prompt_len=64 decode_rate=35 token_budget=512 batch=879
kernel_select: xformers_cuda -> cutlass_int8
kv_cache: miss (cold) first_chunk=128
latency: p50=120ms p95=280ms p99=380ms
```

Rachel: That kernel transition is suspicious — cutlass_int8 wins on long steady decodes but regresses on many small sequences when mixed.

Leo: The timing aligns with PR#4128 rollout yesterday. Any queue policy changes there?

Mikhail: Yes, PR#4128 changed the batcher from FIFO-with-buckets to a weighted-token-fill policy. I noted a subtle interaction with decode-rate bucketing in the review but it slipped.

Anika: Impact summary: customers saw intermittent latency spikes during peak. Root cause seems to be slow-decode short prompts being batched with medium prompts, hitting token_budget too late.

Jamie: Quick config idea to mitigate while we investigate:
```
prompt_buckets: [short:0-80, med:81-512, long:513+]
decode_buckets: [fast:>60, normal:30-60, slow:<30]
queue_policy: prefer_same_decode_rate=true
token_budget_targets: short=256 med=1024 long=2048
```

Rachel: prefer_same_decode_rate=true should reduce harmful mixing. Also lowering short token_budget to 256 makes small sessions dispatch earlier.

Mikhail: Ran local sim matrix:
- baseline (pre-PR4128): throughput ~12.4k tok/s, p99=220ms
- post-PR4128 without tweak: throughput ~9.1k tok/s, p99=380ms
- with prefer_same_decode_rate + budgets: throughput ~11.9k tok/s, p99=230ms

Jamie: Nice improvement. What about KV-cache warmup? Many short prompts are first-in-session and suffer cold KV misses.

Mikhail: Cold KV adds ~18% per-token cost. For slow-short inputs, the right move is to short-circuit and dispatch immediately (lower token_budget) rather than wait to aggregate.

Rachel: Suggest adding an explicit short-circuit: if decode_rate < 25 tok/s and prompt_len < 100 -> immediate dispatch. Also tag for tracing.

Mikhail: Implemented branch batcher/short-slow-shortcircuit. Local perf: p99=215ms, throughput ~12.0k tok/s, kernel_fallback_rate down ~4%.

Leo: Plan to A/B on a canary region. Router CPU will increase a bit due to extra classification work — watch that.

Anika: Rollout plan: canary -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% over 24h with metric gates: p99, tokens/sec, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_miss_rate. Auto rollback on regression.

infra-bot: deploy job started: ci/continuous-batcher/shortcircuit-20260306 -> staging

Rachel: Also request that model-quality regression tests run during canary (some of these heuristics can change batching order and affect randomness in decode).

Mikhail: Will attach kernel_select logs and KV hit traces to the canary run. Also enabling additional perf sampling for the first 2h.

Leo: Added alerts: p99>300ms for 5m -> auto rollback; kernel_fallback_rate>8% -> page oncall.

Anika: Follow-ups assigned: @Mikhail implement rollout + observability hooks, @Jamie run canary and collect traces, @Rachel validate outputs for drift, @Leo monitor infra. Keep me posted.

Jamie: Thanks all :thumbsup: We'll capture traces during canary and iterate. Closing thread until canary results.
